title: Holy, and True, and Righteous Lord
description: Holy, and True, and Righteous Lord in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 393.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre (8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Ho-ly, and true, and right-eous Lord, I wait to prove thy per-fect will, Be mind-ful of thy gra-cious word, And stamp me with thy Spi-rit's seal.

lines: Holy, and true, and righteous Lord,
I wait to prove thy perfect will,
Be mindful of thy gracious word,
And stamp me with thy Spirit's seal.
And all I am shall sink and die,
Confound, o'erpower me by thy grace,
I would be by myself abhorred;
All might, all majesty, all praise,
All glory, be to Christ my Lord
Now let me gain perfection's height,
Now let me into nothing fall;
Be less than nothing in thy sight,
And feel that Christ is all in all!

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
